card.name: Zamba
card.era: 19th century (derived from Peruvian zamacueca via Chilean cueca)
card.tagline: Elegant northwestern courtship dance of waving white handkerchiefs.
card.profile: Zamba is a slow, elegant couples folk dance and music genre of northwestern Argentina (Salta, Tucumán). In 6/8, couples circle each other without touching, waving white handkerchiefs (pañuelos) to enact a poetic courtship of invitation, acceptance, and gentle rejection; women also work their wide skirts. It is played on guitar and bombo legüero, sometimes with violin (English Wikipedia; Dale Folklore). It derives from the Peruvian zamacueca and shares elements with the cueca.
card.insight: Often called the 'queen' of Argentine folk dances and once considered the national dance, zamba is a centerpiece of festivals like Cosquín; its name comes from the colonial term 'zambo' (mixed ancestry), distinct from Brazilian samba (English Wikipedia).
